title: Bonjour tout le monde!
oneGoal: Students will recognize and respond to basic French greetings
decisionPoints: How are students feeling about French today?
What visual supports are most needed?
How much repetition do individuals need?
progression: This is the foundation lesson introducing students to French sounds and basic interaction

title: Je m'appelle...
oneGoal: Students will understand and attempt to say their name in French
decisionPoints: Which students are ready to speak vs. listen only?
How can we use name cards as visual support?
Should we extend practice time or move forward?
progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by adding personal identity to greeting interactions

title: Comment ça va?
oneGoal: Students will recognize feelings words and simple responses
decisionPoints: What emotions are students showing today?
Which feeling words resonate most with the group?
How can we connect to their current mood?
progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by extending personal sharing beyond names to feelings

title: Mes couleurs préférées
oneGoal: Students will identify and name basic colors in French
decisionPoints: Which colors are students naturally drawn to?
Should we use real objects or pictures for color practice?
How can we incorporate movement with color learning?
progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by adding descriptive vocabulary to personal expression

title: Ma famille
oneGoal: Students will recognize family member words and relate to their own family
decisionPoints: How do we honor different family structures?
Which students might share about their families?
Should we use photos or drawings for family sharing?
progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by expanding personal vocabulary to include important people

title: J'aime, je n'aime pas
oneGoal: Students will express simple preferences using 'j'aime'
decisionPoints: What foods/activities will students connect with most?
How can we use thumbs up/down for non-verbal responses?
Should we focus on likes only or introduce dislikes?
progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by giving students language to express personal preferences

title: Les nombres magiques
oneGoal: Students will recognize and count to 5 in French
decisionPoints: Should we use fingers, objects, or songs for counting?
Which students are ready to count independently?
How can we make numbers feel playful and magical?
progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by adding mathematical vocabulary to their French toolkit

title: Mon corps en français
oneGoal: Students will identify basic body parts in French
decisionPoints: How much movement can we incorporate safely?
Which body parts do students already know in English?
Should we sing or use action games for practice?
progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by connecting numbers to countable body parts and physical awareness

title: Dans ma classe
oneGoal: Students will name common classroom objects in French
decisionPoints: Which objects are most important in our daily routine?
Should we label items or play pointing games?
How can we connect this to classroom management?
progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by expanding vocabulary to their immediate environment

title: Écouter et comprendre
oneGoal: Students will demonstrate listening comprehension through actions
decisionPoints: Which commands are students most ready to follow?
Should we use Simon Says or story-based instructions?
How can we support students who need more processing time?
progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by practicing all previous vocabulary through listening activities

title: Sons et rythmes
oneGoal: Students will identify French sounds and rhythm patterns
decisionPoints: Which songs or chants resonate most with students?
Should we use instruments or body percussion?
How can we highlight French pronunciation patterns?
progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by focusing specifically on phonological awareness through music

title: Je peux parler français
oneGoal: Students will demonstrate confidence in using learned French vocabulary
decisionPoints: Which students are ready to speak more independently?
Should we do partner or whole group sharing?
How can we celebrate all levels of French use?
progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by encouraging students to use all learned vocabulary confidently

title: Montrer ce que je sais
oneGoal: Students will demonstrate their French learning through chosen activities
decisionPoints: Which assessment format works best for each student?
Should students choose how to show their learning?
How can we make assessment feel celebratory?
progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by providing opportunities for students to showcase their French growth

title: Célébrer notre français
oneGoal: Students will reflect on and celebrate their French learning journey
decisionPoints: How do students want to celebrate their learning?
Which French words or phrases are they most proud of?
Should we invite others to see our French skills?
progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by consolidating all learning and building positive associations with French

title: Jeux de français
oneGoal: Students will practice vocabulary through games and play
decisionPoints: Which games do students enjoy most?
Should we play competitive or collaborative games?
How can we rotate through different game types?
progression: Builds on Lesson 14 by applying learned French in playful, low-pressure contexts

title: Histoires en français
oneGoal: Students will enjoy and respond to simple French stories
decisionPoints: Which stories capture student interest most?
Should we act out stories or just listen?
How can students participate in storytelling?
progression: Builds on Lesson 15 by experiencing French in narrative contexts with familiar vocabulary

title: Chansons et danses
oneGoal: Students will participate in French songs and movement activities
decisionPoints: Which songs get students most engaged?
Should we focus on singing or movement?
How can shy students participate comfortably?
progression: Builds on Lesson 16 by combining physical movement with French rhythm and vocabulary

title: Art en français
oneGoal: Students will create art while using French vocabulary
decisionPoints: Which art activities allow for French conversation?
Should we focus on color words or other vocabulary?
How can we display student French learning through art?
progression: Builds on Lesson 17 by integrating French vocabulary into creative expression

title: Français partout
oneGoal: Students will discover French in their world beyond the classroom
decisionPoints: Where do students see French in their community?
Should we take a virtual or real French exploration?
How can families be involved in this discovery?
progression: Builds on Lesson 18 by connecting classroom French to the broader world

title: Au revoir pour maintenant
oneGoal: Students will reflect on their French journey and look forward to continued learning
decisionPoints: How do students want to say goodbye to this unit?
What French goals do they have for the future?
Should we create something to remember this learning?
progression: Builds on Lesson 19 by creating closure while maintaining excitement for future French learning
